scope: Research-only three-program comparison: broad allele accessibility vs within-individual viable assembly, researcher-assisted recoding rescue, new adaptive function, and independent lineage reproductive closure.
search_gap: Bounded original-primary search found no verified independent non-Mollicutes total-genome transplantation into a genome-inactivated cell with first-founder negative-survivor exclusion; not exhaustive absence proof.

studies.citation: Khetrapal V, Ow Yong LA, Lim SJM, Chen SL. Development of mass allelic exchange, a technique to enable sexual genetics in Escherichia coli. PNAS 119:e2105458119 (2022).
studies.evidence_grade: E2 original open main Results/Discussion/Methods and figure descriptions, indexed article accessible with intermittent PMC browser challenge; no supplementary/raw data E3 reanalysis
studies.rights: CC BY 4.0 published primary, independent critical paraphrase only; no source experimental sequences, harmful procedures or figures reproduced
studies.program: Singapore National University / Genome Institute of Singapore
studies.measured_unit: 353 selected laboratory-derived E. coli hybrid clones in analyzed collection (not independent abiotic founder lineages); 267 clones with single main recombination block
positive_results: Across a screened arrayed hybrid library donor-origin alleles cover 96% of recipient E. coli chromosome positions in at least one clone (union, not one whole genome replaced)
Sequenced donor-genome tracts approximately 16 to 1780 kilobases across clones with 298 kb median
Donor-derived already existing host-cell interaction phenotype causally linked to a transferred locus within otherwise living E. coli
negatives_limits: Study does not provide joint 96% whole-genome replacement in a single cloned bacterium
Designed recombination and researcher selection relied on living source and recipient cells; laboratory inheritance not abiotic origin
Transferred phenotype existed in biological donor rather than emerging as a wholly new evolved ecological capability
Methodological generalization to other bacterial genera not demonstrated
Clones are selected outcomes and do not quantify all original failed genotype combinations or prospective ecological descendant fitness
founder_scaffold: Already living donor and recipient E. coli
Operator engineered genetic exchange and selective readout
studies.program_independence: Distinct from 2023 Cologne Bacillus and 2026 Harvard recoding labs; different endpoint, not same-result replication

studies.citation: Förster M, Rathmann I, Yüksel M, Power JJ, Maier B. Genome-wide transformation reveals extensive exchange across closely related Bacillus species. Nucleic Acids Research 51:12352–12366 (2023).
studies.evidence_grade: E2 original publisher-indexed Methods, Results/figures, Discussion, license; some full-page open requests fail, but original main sections accessible; no independent raw-data reanalysis
studies.rights: OUP NAR original CC BY-NC 4.0 (different from prior preprint license); critical paraphrase only
studies.program: University of Cologne / Berenike Maier research group
founder_scaffold: Living B. subtilis recipients engineered for inducible competence
Operator-supplied donor DNA, 20 laboratory-managed uptake cycles
Viable colony selection between cycles; sequencing after cycles 10 and 20

experimental_units.assay_ascertainment: Nonviable or very slow non-colony-forming hybrids excluded from assessed populations; not all initial donors/founders

positive_results: Across pooled studied hybrid strains at least 96% of recipient Bacillus core genes accessible to replacement by alleles from B. spizizenii
137 core genes remained without observed replacements among pooled tested samples, not proven inaccessible
For matched laboratory genome-uptake regime, core-genome replacement rates decrease with donor-recipient sequence divergence
negatives_limits: Cross-genus Geobacillus transfer not detected in window, not a universal impossibility proof

For B. atrophaeus original describes very few replacement events in five of eight assayed strains, with clustering in regions of higher similarity (do not rephrase as exactly five positive or negative lineages)
Mean competition fitness not significantly changed among surviving assayed colonies, but tails broaden and individual beneficial/deleterious variants exist
Excluded nonviable and slow overnight-colony failures mean minimal selection is not the absence of viability selection
96% union of accessible core positions across 42 pooled strains is not 96% replacement in any one descendant, and no origin from nonliving inputs
A known same-team earlier transformation study added selection and yielded different rates; do not count as external E3 replication
studies.conflict: No conflicts of interest declared by original
studies.deposited_original_data: NCBI SRA PRJNA987405; Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.8273150; not downloaded or executed

studies.citation: Nyerges A, Chiappino-Pepe A, Budnik B et al. Probing the limits of genetic recoding using multi-omics-guided evolution. Nature Communications 17:5311 (2026).
studies.evidence_grade: E2 full original peer-reviewed published Results/Methods/Discussion/figures/licensing; no supplements/raw omics/code independent repetition
studies.rights: Original Nature Communications CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; do not adapt paper/figures; only original critical paraphrase
studies.program: Harvard Medical School / Church and Nyerges collaborations; GenScript and other research partners; separate original endpoint from 2022/2023 groups
founder_scaffold: Living engineered E. coli lineages from viable cellular ancestors
Human-directed DNA synthesis, genome-segment editing, transcription/proteomics interpretation and directed lab-selection rounds
Operator growth, engineering and transfer; no initial abiotic-cell bootstrap
positive_results: Fully designed synthetic sequence produced as many DNA segments; six partially recoded viable strains constructed, largest 45.8% target synthetic genome in a single E. coli
Full design targets 57 codons, but complete 57-codon living Ec_Syn57 genome not assembled in one viable strain in this paper
Multi-omics-guided lab-debugging identified ways to recover growth phenotype in impaired partial target region
Reported recovery from 110.6 ± 5.83 min to 64.8 ± 3.09 min doubling in one impaired-strain versus selected-variant comparison
negatives_limits: Some synonymous recodings were lethal or impaired growth, despite nominal amino-acid equivalence
Genome synthesis errors, transposition and escape through unreplaced parental DNA demanded investigator interventions
Partially recoded strains >2.2% synthetic target sequence lost tested minimal-medium growth under reported conditions
Remaining full-genome steps unfinished; other paper's Syn57 genome belongs to separate study and cannot be attributed here
Restored phenotype localized to selected engineered segment/strain and lab conditions, not a newly evolved autonomous cellular repair strategy
Estimated variant search volume, partial strain count and parent comparison not independent E3 organism origins
studies.program_independence: One large collaboration with disclosed overlapping interests but distinct lab program; not proof of three independent de novo cell bootstraps
studies.disclosures: Nyerges directed-evolution patent; Harvard provisional Ec_Syn57 patent including Nyerges/Church; named commercial GenScript employees; Church founder equity interests

cross_study_conclusions: 2022 arrayed allele coverage / 2023 pooled lineages / 2026 partial synthetic genome fraction are incompatible denominators and cannot be summed
Existing donor trait transference is not novel beneficial capability originating after selection

Viable laboratory genetic variants and genuine heritable sequence are established, but full abiotic cellular boot, internal constructor genesis, and unattended independent lineage ecology are unverified
All three programs independently studied distinct genetic-variation questions; none replicated another's full causal endpoint
review_limitations: Not a systematic exhaustive negative evidence search
Original full-main methods read but no raw datasets or supplemental reprocessing
Three independent lab programs, not E3 replication of the same experimental result
No laboratory or computational scientific experiments conducted
release_gate: Exact reviewed PR-head syntax/catalog/unittest CI; main and PR head unchanged at expected-head merge; separately verify post-merge main push CI. Interactive write does not prove scheduled custodian write authority.
